question: In December 2023 the European Commission published a guide on good electoral practices for persons with disabilities, which aimed to make electoral processes in the EU more accessible for people with disabilities.

According to the European Disability Forum, the guide marks a step towards electoral accessibility but fails to fully address the fundamental inequalities terms of voting and eligibility rights facing persons with disabilities in the EU Member States. The persistence of legal obstacles, particularly for persons with psychosocial disabilities, is a major concern.
What does the Commission therefore intend to do to eliminate inequalities in the voting and eligibility rights of persons with disabilities in the EU Member States?
answer: It is the competence and responsibility of Member States to organise elections according to relevant international commitments, including to ensure that persons with disabilities can participate.

The Commission supports inclusive electoral participation and accessibility of elections (1), including by raising awareness about the rights of persons with disabilities (2) and facilitating the exchange of good electoral practices in the framework of the European Cooperation Network on Elections.

The EU funds EU-level disability organisations to raise awareness, advocate for rights, and improve the capacity of their member organisations. The guide (3) referred to by the Honourable Member was prepared in close cooperation with Member States in the framework of the European Cooperation Network on Elections, and by consulting different stakeholders.

The guide reflects measures taken by Member States to address the obstacles faced by citizens with disabilities when interacting with the electoral environment and to ensure the effectiveness of their electoral rights. It aims to support further discussions among Member States’ relevant authorities (4), including in the framework of the European Cooperation Network on Elections.
On 13 December 2023, the Commission adopted a recommendation on inclusive and resilient elections (5), as part of the Defence of Democracy Package.

Among others, it complements the foregoing guide and encourages Member States to prevent and remove the barriers persons with disabilities encounter when participating in elections, including the blanket removal of electoral rights of persons with intellectual and psycho-social disabilities without individual assessment and possibility of judicial review.
As outlined in the strategy for the Rights of Persons with Disabilities 2021-2030, it is essential to ensure that persons with disabilities can participate in elections.

The European Commission regularly organises events to raise awareness on the importance of the political participation of persons with disabilities, such as the high-level event on elections (23-24 October 2023), which included a dedicated session on ‘Best practices for ensuring electoral rights for people with disabilities’.

Guide of good electoral practices in Member States addressing participation of citizens with disabilities in the electoral process — Commission Staff Working Document SWD(2023) 408 final (https://commission.europa.eu/system/files/2023-12/SWD_2023_408_1_EN_document_travail_service_part1_v4.pdf).

The Spanish Presidency of the Council showed great interest in supporting the electoral rights of persons with disabilities and prepared a declaration which was supported by many Member States, rpdiscapacidad.gob.es/documentos/Noticias/DeclarationRighttoVoteENG.pdf Commission Recommendation of 12.12.
